Day 2 / Claude Code

Build and run yesterday’s program

Paste this into the Claude Code session you just opened.

Build the Day 1 game from this checkout using the existing build script. Leave the source unchanged. If the build fails, stop and show me the error. If it succeeds, launch the freshly built PRG in VICE with autostart. Leave the emulator open so I can test the disk pickup.

You can also run it yourself in Command Prompt or PowerShell.

1. Build the game
.\build.cmd
2. After a successful build, run it
x64sc -autostart .\build\rescue.prg
Day 2 / CorgiMind

Open Claude Design on your desktop

We’ll design both rooms here. Paste the brief below into Claude Design to sketch the two routes Tank can take.

Design two original single-screen rooms for Tank’s Disk Rescue, a Commodore 64 digging game. Use the same limited palette, grid size and tile legend in both. Include Tank the corgi, a collectible disk, diggable dirt, a crate, solid walls, open space and an exit. A offers a short dig beneath a supported crate with a longer way around. B uses a winding approach with the crate guarding the return. Show both unannotated rooms first, then a separate route overlay for each. Keep sprites readable at small size. Give me fixed-width text maps and a legend to hand to the developer.
Day 2 / Claude Design

Room sketches with Fable 5.2

I sketched these two rooms in Claude Design with Fable 5.2 before the stream. Trace a route from Tank to the disk in each sketch. Where would you dig first?

Day 2 / Room selection

Which room should we build?

Claude Design

Hand off the selected room to Claude Code

I’ll choose a room in Claude Design, then ask it to prepare the map and tile legend for Claude Code.

Prepare a handoff for Claude Code for the room I selected. Include its letter and palette, grid dimensions, a fixed-width text map and a tile legend. Mark Tank, the disk, the crate, its support and the exit. Trace the intended route. Call out any detail you inferred from the drawing so I can confirm it.

Compare the map with the sketch. Copy the handoff text, including the map’s line breaks.

Claude Code / Plan Mode

Bring the design back to Claude Code

Return to the Claude Code session in the game repo. Enter Plan Mode. Paste this prompt and append the handoff from Claude Design in the same message.

Read the design handoff below. Check the map dimensions, tile symbols and route against our Day 1 renderer. Check that the score has room. Flag anything the C64 cannot display as drawn and suggest the smallest adjustment. Outline a room-rendering pass and a Fire-to-start pass. Wait for my approval before editing.

Keep the selected sketch visible while you review the plan.

Trace the route before coding

Day 2 / CorgiMind

Press Fire to start

Implement pass two. Show a title screen for Tank’s Disk Rescue with the actual controls. Wait for a fresh joystick Fire press or a displayed keyboard alternative, then enter the room from the approved handoff. Keep movement and falling crates for Day 3. Build and report the PRG path. Give me the manual input checks.
Let chat write the first test
  1. Hands off
  2. Tap Fire once
  3. Hold Fire through startup

Say “You get the first test. Type 1, 2 or 3, and tell me what you expect to see. If I’m already holding Fire when the game starts, should that count as a new press?”

Show Leave the choices up during the build. Read one prediction aloud, switch to VICE and launch the new PRG with that input. For 3, hold Fire before launch, then release and press again. Ask, “Did we get what you predicted?”

Show the title screen on stream, press Fire, and hold on the room reveal.
